work.text: In the Rape of Europa Tiepolo identified himself not with the most famous painter of antiquity but, audaciously, with the ruler of the gods.

moment.text: At the end of the 17th century things began to change dramatically, and for much of the 18th century Venetian painters were in remarkable demand all over Europe, even as the city itself declined and was a much reduced market, in particular for large works

matters.text: [In 1719,] Tiepolo married noblewoman Maria Cecilia Guardi, sister of two contemporary Venetian painters, Francesco and Giovanni Antonio Guardi.
it seems plausible that Tiepolo gave Agenor's proud daughter, the beautiful Phoenician princess kidnapped by Zeus, the features of his young wife.
